Granit Xhaka was central to their early set-piece pressure, delivering several dangerous corners that tested the Chelsea backline. The deadlock was finally broken in the 25th minute when Trai Hume connected with a cross from Luke O’Nien following a key pass by Robin Roefs . In the 50th minute, disaster struck for the Blues when Malo Gusto inadvertently turned the ball into his own net, doubling Sunderland 's advantage. However, Chelsea responded almost immediately. Red Card and a Frantic Finish Just as momentum seemed to shift, Chelsea suffered a significant blow in the 62nd minute. Wesley Fofana , who had been booked only minutes earlier, received a second yellow card and was sent off. Despite being down to ten men, Chelsea pushed forward, introducing fresh legs like Liam Delap . The final minutes were marred by a flurry of yellow cards for players such as Enzo Fernandez , Joao Pedro , and Cole Palmer as tensions boiled over. Ultimately, Sunderland held firm in front of 47,155 fans to secure the victory in a match defined by its physical edge and late-game drama.
